source: ការថែរក្សាដំណាំធូរេនក្នុងពេលដល់ផ្កាផ្កា និងផ្លែ (Care of Durian During Flowering and Fruiting), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Department of Agricultural Extension, Cambodia Agriculture Sector Investment Project, loan 2022-CAM[SF], 2007, 4pp
text:
This short MAFF extension leaflet focuses specifically on the flowering-and-fruiting period, which it describes as the most delicate and risk-prone stage of durian care, since problems at this stage directly determine how many, and how good, the fruit will be. It covers four linked practices: preparation of the tree ahead of flowering, removing excess/weak flower clusters, removing excess set fruit, and removing excess leaves competing with flowers/fruit for the tree's resources.

Tree preparation ahead of flowering: the tree should enter the flowering period with balanced nutrition (not nitrogen-heavy, which favors leaf growth over flowering) and without pest or disease pressure on the canopy, since a stressed or unhealthy tree flowers poorly and holds fruit poorly.

Flower-cluster thinning: after the flower buds appear, remove flower clusters growing on weak or thin branches, keep only well-spaced clusters on strong branches, and if two flower clusters occur close together on the same strong branch, keep the more vigorous of the two and remove the other, so the tree's resources concentrate on fewer, stronger flower sets.

Fruit-set thinning, described here in the same three rounds as Source A of this batch: round 1 about 3-4 weeks after flowering (removing malformed or crowded young fruit, targeting roughly 50% removal of the initial set), round 2 about 6-8 weeks after flowering (removing fruit with insect damage or split husks), and round 3, a final thinning pass a bit later, removing any remaining fruit that is small, crowded, or oddly shaped, keeping only well-spaced, healthy fruit with room to develop fully.

The leaflet also gives a specific fruiting-period fertilizer note: 4-16-24-24 at 2-4kg per tree, applied at this stage, matching the fruit-development fertilizer program described in Source A.

Leaf management: some competing new leaf growth should be pruned back during heavy flowering/fruiting so the tree channels energy into the developing fruit rather than splitting it with a simultaneous vegetative flush, and any dead, diseased, weak, or crossing branches should be removed at the same time to keep the canopy healthy through the demanding fruiting period.

The leaflet closes by naming the Department of Agricultural Legislation and Extension Techniques (ក្រុមការងារផ្សព្វផ្សាយបច្ចេកវិទ្យាកសិកម្ម) as the compiling/publishing body, under the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, with support noted as loan 2022-CAM[SF].
